{"status": "success", "summary": "Started a stdlib HTTP service on 127.0.0.1:8765, really curl'd it, wrote the true body to service.txt, then stopped it and confirmed it was gone.

1) Files written in the workspace:
- service.py (946 B): python3 stdlib http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler + ThreadingHTTPServer, HTTP/1.1, GET /health -> 200 with body b"p6-service-ok" (Content-Length 13); any other path -> 404. Logs to stdout.
- service.txt (13 B): real curl response body, content exactly "p6-service-ok" (no trailing newline), sha256 79cd5fda49217cbebaa4a72e23782d8c53e26cd288b17bfef0e4c7174acf4cf9 — identical to `printf 'p6-service-ok' | sha256sum`.
- service.pid (PID 320), service.nohup (server log) kept as evidence.

2) Start (background/detached, shell did not block):
`nohup python3 service.py > service.nohup 2>&1 < /dev/null & echo $! > service.pid; disown`
Result: pid=320, `ps` showed `320 S python3 service.py`; log line "listening on http://127.0.0.1:8765". The process was still alive in a later, separate shell call, so it was genuinely detached, not a foreground wait.

3) Access (real curl):
`curl -sS -i --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8765/health` -> `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, Server BaseHTTP/0.6 Python/3.13.15, Content-Type text/plain; charset=utf-8, Content-Length 13, body `p6-service-ok`.
`curl -sS --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8765/health > service.txt` -> curl_exit=0, 13 bytes, content `p6-service-ok`.

4) Stop and post-check:
`kill 320` -> poll: "STOPPED: pid 320 no longer alive".
Post-stop curl `http://127.0.0.1:8765/health` -> `curl: (7) Failed to connect ... Could not connect to server` (curl_exit=7); `ss -ltnp | grep 8765` -> no listener on 8765. So the service really was running during the check and really is stopped now.
